description: THE ZERO-RATE GUARD: A LARGE BALANCE, A RATE OF 0.00, AND THEREFORE NOTHING WRITTEN AT ALL. This is the negative half of the guard at app/cbl/CBACT04C.cbl:214 and the exact mirror of case08. There DIS-INT-RATE was 15.00 and the computed amount truncated to 0.00, and a 350-byte record WAS written; here DIS-INT-RATE is 0.00 against a balance of 1930.00 and nothing is written at all. Read together the two cases pin the guard's subject beyond argument: IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0 tests the RATE and never the computed AMOUNT. Either case alone leaves that ambiguous - case08 by itself cannot rule out an implementation that ignores the rate and writes on every path, and this case by itself cannot rule out one that gates on the amount, since a zero rate makes the amount zero too. Only the pair separates them, and the pair is the point. WHAT IS SKIPPED, STATEMENT BY STATEMENT. :213-217 is PERFORM 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE / IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0 / PERFORM 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST / PERFORM 1400-COMPUTE-FEES / END-IF. With the rate at 0.00 the condition is FALSE and BOTH performs are skipped. Each consequence is asserted rather than assumed. (1) 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST at :462-470 does not run, so the COMPUTE at :464-465 never executes and the ADD WS-MONTHLY-INT TO WS-TOTAL-INT at :467 never executes: WS-TOTAL-INT stays at 0.00. (2) 1300-B-WRITE-TX at :473-515 is reachable ONLY from :468, inside the paragraph that was skipped, so WRITE FD-TRANFILE-REC at :500 never executes and the generated-transaction output ends the run empty. (3) ADD 1 TO WS-TRANID-SUFFIX at :474 therefore never executes either. WS-TRANID-SUFFIX is PIC 9(06) VALUE 0 and stays at zero, so the STRING at :476-480 never composes a TRAN-ID and NO sixteen-byte identifier is formed anywhere in this run: the one case08 writes appears NOWHERE in this file, and its presence would mean the guard had been evaluated on the amount instead of the rate. The assertion is spelled out because 'no record written' and 'a record written with a zero amount' are two different observable outcomes and only one of them is correct here. (4) 1400-COMPUTE-FEES at :518-520 is not invoked at all. 1400-COMPUTE-FEES AND GATE G26, IN ITS STRONGEST AVAILABLE FORM. The paragraph at :518-520 is a header, the comment '* To be implemented' and EXIT - zero statements. Every other case in this folder asserts that invoking it changes nothing; this case asserts something stronger, because the PERFORM at :216 sits INSIDE the guard. The stub is not merely empty here, it is never reached - so a fee record, a fee field or a fee message would have to arrive by a path that does not exist, which makes any fee artefact doubly impossible. Implementing fees would be a new feature and a parity violation (practice B5). TWO DELIBERATELY EMPTY EXPECTATIONS, EACH ARGUED RATHER THAN LEFT BLANK (practice B1). An empty expectation and an unfinished case look identical in a file, so both of this case's are justified in full. A NOTE ON THE MEMBER NAMES FIRST (practice B4): the brief for this case asks for a member called expectedRecords. parity.ParityCase declares no such member and is annotated @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = false), so that name is not merely unconventional here, it is unloadable. The two real members are used instead, exactly as every other case in this folder uses them - expectedWrites for what the unit wrote and expectedFinalState for what each dataset holds afterwards - together with expectedDatasets, which states the one thing neither row list can. The correction is recorded rather than applied silently. (A) THE GENERATED-TRANSACTION OUTPUT HOLDS ZERO ROWS. expectedWrites is EMPTY, which asserts that nothing was written to any dataset anywhere; and SYSTRAN is additionally pinned on the WRITES channel at rowCount 0 with recordLength 350, which is the more specific and stronger statement: the dataset was OPENED and produced nothing. The two are not redundant. An empty row list cannot distinguish a job that opened its output and wrote no record from one that never opened it, and here the difference is real - :309 is OPEN OUTPUT and :597 is its CLOSE, both of which succeed, so the run is entirely clean and the dataset simply ends up empty. 350 is CVTRA05Y's declared width and app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl:39's RECFM=F,LRECL=350; pinning it is how an empty output's identity is pinned at all, since it has no row whose width could be checked. (B) THE ACCOUNT MASTER RECEIVES ZERO REWRITES. ACCTFILE appears in expectedFinalState byte-identical to its seed, and that is the assertion 'no REWRITE happened' rather than an omission. Two INDEPENDENT reasons, stated separately because they fail independently. FIRST, control flow: 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT is reached from :196 only on an account break where WS-FIRST-TIME is NOT 'Y', and with a single input record this break IS the first, so :195 routes to :198 and merely flips the flag. Its only other call site is the ELSE at :219-220, which is unreachable dead code: the enclosing PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' at :188 makes the IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' at :189 always true, so the last - and here only - account group is never flushed to the master. That is the legacy behaviour and practice B5 forbids 'fixing' it; a run that added an end-of-file flush would alter the account master and fail this case. SECOND, arithmetic: even had a rewrite occurred, WS-TOTAL-INT is 0.00, so ADD WS-TOTAL-INT TO ACCT-CURR-BAL at :352 would have left the balance at 1930.00 unchanged and the two MOVE 0 statements at :353-354 would have re-zeroed two spans that already read 00000000000{ in this record. TCATBALF, XREFFILE, XREFFIL1 and DISCGRP are likewise unchanged: this program reads all four and rewrites none of them. WHAT DID HAPPEN - WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE EMPTY OUTPUT A PROOF RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE. All five files are opened successfully and in the source's order - TCATBALF at :236, XREF-FILE at :254, DISCGRP-FILE at :272, ACCOUNT-FILE with OPEN I-O at :291 and TRANSACT-FILE with OPEN OUTPUT at :309 - and all five are closed successfully at :524, :543, :561, :579 and :597, so not one of the ten open- and close-failure messages is emitted. The category-balance row was genuinely read at :326 and displayed at :193, which is the second of the three expected lines and proves the row reached the loop body. The account read at :202-203 succeeded and the alternate-key cross-reference read at :204-205 succeeded, because BOTH sit inside the account-break block at :194-206 and OUTSIDE the guard at :214: a card number was fetched and then never used, its only consumer being MOVE XREF-CARD-NUM TO TRAN-CARD-NUM at :495 inside the paragraph that never ran. The disclosure-group read at :416 succeeded with FILE STATUS '00'. Only THEN did the guard fail. Every one of those steps is asserted - four of them by the datasets pinned in expectedFinalState, one by the displayed line, and the '00' read by the ABSENCE of the two lines a miss would have produced. THE DISCLOSURE-GROUP READ SUCCEEDS ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT - GATE G47's '00' OUTCOME. :210-212 build the key from ACCT-GROUP-ID, TRANCAT-CD and TRANCAT-TYPE-CD in that order, which here is 'ZEROAPR   ' + '01' + '0001'. That key is present, so the READ at :416 returns '00', the INVALID KEY arm at :417-419 does not fire, and the IF DISCGRP-STATUS = '23' test at :436 is false so 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE at :443-460 is never performed. This is the same first-read-succeeds shape case05 establishes, and it is deliberately the OPPOSITE of the '23'-then-DEFAULT path that case01, case03 and case08 exercise: between them the folder covers both outcomes of the same READ. THE ZEROAPR BLOCK, VERIFIED RATHER THAN TRUSTED. app/data/ASCII/discgrp.txt is exactly three blocks of seventeen rows keyed 'A000000000', 'DEFAULT   ' and 'ZEROAPR   ' - 51 rows BY DESIGN, never an off-by-one and never to be 'corrected' - and all 51 are seeded here unmodified, so the lookup had to find its row among the whole file rather than in a hand-picked slice. Every one of the seventeen ZEROAPR keys - 01/0001 through 01/0004, 02/0001 through 02/0003, 03/0001 through 03/0003, 04/0001 through 04/0003, 05/0001, 06/0001, 06/0002 and 07/0001 - carries DIS-INT-RATE 00000{, which is 0.00. All seventeen were checked before this case was written, because a single non-zero row among them would invert its entire premise. The row read here is 'ZEROAPR   01000100000{' followed by its 28-byte trailing span. THE KEY-WIDTH TRAP, MEASURED (practice B11). app/cpy/CVTRA02Y.cpy declares DIS-GROUP-KEY as X(10) + X(02) + 9(04) = SIXTEEN bytes, so DIS-INT-RATE S9(04)V99 occupies 1-based bytes 17-22. The genuinely SEVENTEEN-byte key is CVTRA01Y's TRAN-CAT-KEY, and because both records total 50 bytes the slip is invisible by width alone. Read at 18-23 instead, this row yields the six characters 0000{0 - an overpunch stranded mid-span - which is not zero and would silently turn this case into a positive one. The rate was read at 17-22. PROVENANCE OF THE TWO MODIFIED SPANS, DISCLOSED IN FULL (practice B12). Neither is fixture-verbatim and neither is dressed up as though it were. (1) THE BALANCE. All FIFTY rows of app/data/ASCII/tcatbal.txt carry TRAN-CAT-BAL 0000000000{ - one distinct value, exhaustively checked - so the shipped fixture cannot exercise this guard meaningfully: at a balance of 0.00 no rate produces interest and an empty output would prove nothing about the rate. The row seeded into TCATBALF is therefore account 00000000007's own fixture row - its 17-byte key 00000000007 + '01' + '0001' and its 22-byte trailing span of zeros, both verbatim - with the balance replaced by 0000019300{, which is 1930.00 at CVTRA01Y's declared S9(09)V99 scale. That figure is not invented: it is account 7's real ACCT-CURR-BAL in acctdata.txt, the twelve bytes 00000001930{, so the amount is fixture-derived even though the row is modified. A LARGE balance was chosen on purpose. It makes the absence of a record unambiguous - had the balance been zero, a correct implementation and one that gates on the amount would both write nothing and the case would assert nothing at all. At 1930.00 any non-zero rate would have produced a record; at the 1.50 the DEFAULT block would have supplied it would have been 2.41. The empty output is therefore attributable to the rate and to nothing else. (2) THE GROUP ID. ACCTFILE carries an overriding explicit row rather than a fixture reference, and EXACTLY ONE FIELD differs from acctdata.txt row 7: ACCT-GROUP-ID at 1-based bytes 113-122 changes from TEN SPACES to 'ZEROAPR' followed by THREE trailing spaces, the seven-character literal padded to its declared PIC X(10). Seven characters differ in the whole 300-byte image, verified by counting them. Everything else is carried through verbatim - the 00000000007 key, the 'Y' active status, ACCT-CURR-BAL 00000001930{, the credit and cash-credit limits, the three date spans including the misspelled ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE at 59-68 whose name is preserved exactly as app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy spells it, both cycle amounts at 00000000000{, ACCT-ADDR-ZIP and the trailing FILLER X(178) as 178 spaces. AND A CORRECTION TO THE FOLDER BRIEF, RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED (practice B4): the override is NECESSARY, because the fixture cannot reach the ZEROAPR block at all. Read mechanically against CVACT01Y, acctdata.txt row 7 leaves ACCT-GROUP-ID EMPTY and holds A000000000 in ACCT-ADDR-ZIP at bytes 103-112 - one field earlier - so MOVE ACCT-GROUP-ID TO FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID at :210 would move spaces, the read at :416 would miss with '23', and the run would fall through to the DEFAULT block, whose 01/0001 rate is 15.00 and which would produce a record. Without the override this case would be case08. A NOTE FOR READERS OF case08 (practices B4, B12). case08's own description records - honestly and correctly at the time it was written - that no case in this folder seeded a zero DIS-INT-RATE and that the guard's FALSE arm was therefore unasserted. THIS case is that arm. It also takes a different route to it than case08 suggested: rather than the DEFAULT block's zero-rate rows, which are reachable only after a '23' miss and a retry, it uses the ZEROAPR block, which is reached on the FIRST read - so the zero rate is asserted with no fallback path in the way, and gate G47's '00' outcome is exercised at the same time. case08 is not edited from here; the divergence is documented instead. NO WALL-CLOCK VALUE IS REACHABLE, SO NONE IS PINNED (practice B7). Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP at :613-626 is performed from exactly one place: :496, inside 1300-B-WRITE-TX. That paragraph never runs here, so TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS are never composed and this case's expectations contain no timestamp of any kind. It is the ONLY case in this folder inherently free of wall-clock values rather than made deterministic by a pinned clock, and the difference is worth naming: elsewhere determinism is achieved, here it is structural. No pinned timestamp literal is added to a record that does not exist. THE JOB PARAMETER IS SUPPLIED, CORRECT AND UNUSED. parmDate is '2022071800', taken verbatim from app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl:22 EXEC PGM=CBACT04C,PARM='2022071800' and received by PARM-DATE PIC X(10) at :178 as character data that is never parsed as a date. It is declared because the job requires it and because omitting it would test the harness rather than the program, but it is consumed in exactly one place - the STRING at :476-480 inside 1300-B-WRITE-TX - so on this path it goes entirely unused. Its correct handling is asserted by the cases that do write a record and is not the subject here. MESSAGES: EXACTLY THREE LINES, AND EVERY ABSENCE IS AN ASSERTION (practice B1). In emission order: the :181 banner, the raw 50-byte DISPLAY TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD at :193 reproducing the seeded row byte for byte at its full width, and the :230 banner. That is all, and an intentionally short expectation has to say why it is short. Absent, each deliberately: 'DISCLOSURE GROUP RECORD MISSING' and 'TRY WITH DEFAULT GROUP CODE' at :418-419, because the first read hit the ZEROAPR block and returned '00'; 'ERROR READING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE' at :431 and 'ERROR READING DEFAULT DISCLOSURE GROUP' at :455, because no error arm is reached and the DEFAULT retry never runs; 'ERROR WRITING TRANSACTION RECORD' at :510, because no write is attempted; 'ERROR RE-WRITING ACCOUNT FILE' at :365, because no rewrite is attempted; 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: ' at :375 and :397, because both keyed reads found their record; and 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at :629 together with the rendered FILE STATUS line, because nothing on this path reaches 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. expectedReturnCode is 0 for that reason and not 12: a zero rate is entirely normal, not an error condition. WIDTHS, FILLER AND SEEDS (gates G19, G21). The ACCTFILE image is 300 bytes, CVACT01Y's declared width, and its trailing FILLER X(178) is emitted as 178 spaces - a total that fails immediately if FILLER is dropped or zero-filled, which is exactly how gate G21 is enforced. The TCATBALF row and the displayed line are each exactly 50 bytes, CVTRA01Y's width. Each cross-reference row is CVACT03Y's 50 bytes in expectedFinalState and 36 in the fixture: the shipped cardxref.txt is 36 bytes per record because it omits CVACT03Y's trailing FILLER X(14), the fixture is NEVER edited and NEVER pre-padded here, and the 14 spaces are supplied once, at seed time, by the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation, which ParityCase.DatasetNormalisation.normaliseSeedRow owns (gate G16, risk R-F). XREFFILE and XREFFIL1 are seeded from the SAME single row - row 21 of cardxref.txt, found by matching XREF-ACCT-ID at 1-based bytes 26-36 against 00000000007 rather than by assuming positional correspondence - because XREFFIL1 is an alternate-index PATH over the same base cluster and not a second dataset; app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl:29-32 opens both in one step, which is the shape gate G45 is about. TRANSACT is output only and is not seeded. EXPLICIT ADDRESSING AND EXPLICIT BYTES (practice B8). Every dataset is addressed by its carddemo.datasets BINDING KEY - TCATBALF, ACCTFILE, XREFFILE, XREFFIL1, DISCGRP and the SYSTRAN output - and never by a fully-qualified mainframe dataset name; no such name appears anywhere in this file, including in this prose, so gate G46 is structural here rather than a matter of care, and ParityCase's binding-key pattern could not accept a dotted name in any event. Every rowIndex is ZERO-BASED and is a position within the seeded dataset, not a line number in the fixture the rows came from; the 51 DISCGRP rows are pinned in ascending record order, which for this already-ascending fixture is file order. Bytes are US-ASCII throughout, matching app/data/ASCII, and never a platform default. The 'ZEROAPR   ' literal is ten characters - seven letters and THREE trailing spaces - counted numerically rather than eyeballed, because a trimmed trailing space would change the key and the read would miss. REFERENCE INPUTS ARE UNTOUCHED (practice B3). Both overrides live inside this JSON. Not one byte of app/cbl, app/cpy, app/jcl or app/data was changed to write this case: acctdata.txt still leaves ACCT-GROUP-ID empty, discgrp.txt is unmodified, tcatbal.txt still carries fifty zero balances and cardxref.txt is still 36 bytes per record. HOW THE UNIT IS REACHED (gate G51): account.AccountInterestCalcJob is invoked at step level through calculateInterest, with no HTTP layer, no JobLauncher, no job repository and no step executor between the assertion and the code. PROVENANCE (practice B12, risk R-A): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of the COBOL paragraphs cross-checked against the CVTRA01Y, CVTRA02Y, CVACT01Y and CVACT03Y byte layouts, the INTCALC.jcl DD and PARM contract, and the real ASCII fixtures. Nothing was captured from, recorded against or replayed from an execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment. GOVERNING RULES: review_rules returns the single line 'No user rules provided.' - that is the entire document. No rule is invented and its absence is not treated as permission to lower the bar; the plan's best-practice substitutes bind instead, and the ones this case turns on are named inline above - B1 for the two argued-empty expectations, B3, B4, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12. GATES OWNED: G15, G16, G18, G19, G21, G26, G45, G46, G47 and G51.
